title: What kind of thing is it, by when it acts?
lede: Two questions name it: what sets it off, and whether it acts once, again as written down, or again decided each time.

cells.gloss: goes off once, at a time set in advance
the clock sets off each run
kept in force: acts at each occasion until withdrawn
a clock repeats only from something written down
it comes again and again, and is decided each time

add.gloss: someone asks for each run of a kept procedure
it runs each time, but acts only when a check finds a reason
a timed check finds its occasion, so it acts at the next check
someone runs it to a calendar, from written steps

renames.why: No clock sets it off: it runs when a session starts, if two days have passed. The registry's README says a blank schedule means no schedule.
It runs when a view that reads it opens, and reads only repos that moved. app/index.html says its old interval was never a schedule.
docs/properties.csv files GitHub's schedule among the events, so the harness counts an hourly cron as event-fired.

web-tools calls a Claude scheduled task a Routine in writers.csv, venues.md, vocabularies.csv and inbound.md; the registry calls it a scheduled task, and budget-drs uses routine for work someone runs to a calendar.

renames.becomes: a word for the box at top left (call 2)
renames.why: The send-later guard calls it a scheduled self check-in, but it goes off once; scheduled here means a clock that sets off each run.
home's 2026-03-17 entry calls it ad hoc because it is used when a question comes up, but it follows the same written steps each time; ad hoc here means decided each time.

open.question: Adopt occasioned for whatever the clock does not set off?
open.why: The scheduled-task registry already defines scheduled as neither someone asking nor something happening, and occasioned names the other half in one word. But the forms codebook in data/ui-units coded each page's occasion as standing, occasioned or inbox from 2026-10-22 and replaced it with job tags on 2026-10-23 (commit 3b9e76670), the day this map was drawn, so occasioned and this poster's standing were both retired in a nearby sense.

open.question: What should a timer set to go off once be called?
open.why: The send-later guard already calls the kind someone asked for a reminder, and a standing instruction refuses the other kind, the PR check-in.

open.question: Retire triggered and periodic as words for when estate work acts?
open.why: Triggered means any start, an event or a condition by turns; periodic's one live use names a crawl that runs when a view opens. Say what sets it off, or say gated. The budget submittal's if-triggered status follows OFM's forms and can stay.

open.question: Keep news-fetch in the scheduled-task registry once it is not called scheduled?
open.why: The registry's README already gives session-start rows a blank schedule and says why their timing matters: news-fetch's feeds drop items after about three days. The row records that risk; the name is what changes.

by: Placed by one reader's hand coding of 33 things across web-tools, home and web-tools-private. No second reader has checked the coding, and the renames are that reader's proposals.
